method: Native Tauri/WebKit pointer capture after a completed framebuffer capture. Guest timeout/cat records Linux input_event structs; od reads each 8-byte payload after its 16-byte timestamp. X11 host input moves17,-9, clicks left, scrolls up once, then holds left while pressing Escape before host button-up.

motion_and_buttons.note: Final button release follows capture exit on Escape, before host button-up. The single wheel action did not reach an integral detent.

wheel.method: Recapture pointer, send three host scroll-up actions, release with Escape

limitations: Native tests cover relative X/Y, left button, vertical wheel and Escape release, not every button or horizontal wheel
Cross-device modifier ordering, failure recovery, coalescing and fractional wheel boundaries tested with mocked IPC and pointer lock
Relative input is affected by host/guest acceleration; absolute cursor synchronization is not claimed
No graphical desktop application interaction or abrupt-disconnect button release guarantee
Full-frame transfer latency remains unsuitable for responsive desktop use
No complete milestone or release qualification
